Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you when you may be experiencing hypertension, but they don't provide actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they need to be calibrated regularly with a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims it can provide full blood pressure measurement without any calibration, citing clinical trial results involving thousands of participants……

「Silent Killer」

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) both pose serious health risks.

Of the two, hypertension is more dangerous, earning the nickname 「silent killer」 because it can cause severe and irreversible damage to your arteries, heart and brain without obvious symptoms. Many people don't discover they have this condition until after a heart attack or stroke.

For older people, regular blood pressure monitoring is ideal. Home upper-arm blood pressure monitors are widely available on the market and very easy to use. However, it would be even better to have an all-day wearable fitness device that provides fully automatic monitoring.

Apple Watch Blood Pressure Feature

With the launch of watchOS 26, five Apple Watch models can now measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models won't give you any readings—they will only issue alerts when possible signs of hypertension are detected. Other devices like the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices on the market can provide actual blood pressure readings, but they require regular calibration using readings from an upper-arm blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup company Vital Signals says its Signal Ring smart ring can achieve accuracy comparable to traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitors without any calibration.

CEO Tom Moss told Bloomberg in an interview that he nearly died from undiagnosed hypertension—an experience that inspired him to found the company.

The Signal Ring opens for pre-order later today, ships in October, priced at US$399 with no subscription required. The companion mobile app displays real-time blood pressure readings and long-term trends (as shown above).

Worth noting: The Oura Ring has not yet received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials show it can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss isn't particularly interested in marketing the Signal Ring to all consumers. He says the feature is best suited for older adults and people assessed by doctors as being at risk of hypertension—the implication being that the Signal Ring may not particularly stand out in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
